content.text:
What kind of story is The Enormous Turnip?

The Enormous Turnip is a story in which the whole family and their animals lend a hand, one after another, to pull up a turnip that has grown impossibly huge. With its repeating refrain of "Heave-ho!", it's a folk tale that joyfully teaches the power of working together.

content.alt: The Enormous Turnip - The original Enormous Turnip story
content.text:
The original Enormous Turnip story

It is a Russian folk tale, and the version retold by Alexei Tolstoy is the most widely known. Its heart is the cumulative, repeating structure in which grandpa → grandma → granddaughter → dog → cat → mouse each grab hold in turn until the turnip is finally pulled free.
content.caption: Strength added one by one

content.alt: The Enormous Turnip - A summary of the Enormous Turnip story
content.text:
A summary of the Enormous Turnip story

When grandpa plants a turnip, it grows impossibly huge. He can't pull it out alone, so grandma, the granddaughter, the dog, and the cat grab hold one after another, but it won't budge — until at last even the tiny mouse lends its strength, and "pop!" out comes the turnip.
content.caption: The result that a small strength made

content.alt: The Enormous Turnip - The moral of The Enormous Turnip
content.text:
The moral of The Enormous Turnip

The heart of it is that even a task too hard to do alone can be accomplished when done together, and even a small strength is precious. Ask, "What if the little mouse hadn't been there?" to talk with your child about how everyone's role matters.
content.caption: A strength that is precious even when small

content.alt: The Enormous Turnip - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Shout "Heave-ho! Heave-ho!" together with your child, louder and louder, while acting out the pulling. Each time another character joins in, it's fun to add a finger and count along. Best suited for ages 3–6.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Enormous Turnip good for?
A. It's best suited for ages 3–6. The cumulative repetition and the "Heave-ho" refrain are especially fun for younger children.

Q. Why is the mouse important?
A. Because it's the last small bit of strength that finally pulls the turnip out. The message is that even a small role is precious.

Q. What activities go well with it?
A. A pulling game together, counting the order of the characters, and talking about "something we all did together" all work well.
